Luxembourg-United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement (1967, with subsequent amending protocols)
Luxembourg-France Double Taxation Agreement (1958, as amended)

Energy Charter Treaty, in force for Luxembourg

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (including by the Law of 25 March 2020 transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners, as amended by the Law of 18 July 2023 restricting public access following the CJEU judgment of 22 November 2022 in joined cases C-37/20 and C-601/20; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended; Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies and on companies' and partnerships' registers, as amended; CSSF Regulation No. 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or other valid government-issued identity document of each founder and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport or identity authority of the country of origin of each founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the country of origin; alternatively Consular Legalization by the Luxembourg Embassy/Consulate where the country of origin is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention of 5 October 1961

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, regulated financial institution, or municipal records authority of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as determined by the country of origin status under the 1961 Hague Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing (or equivalent excerpt from the commercial register) for any corporate founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official companies registry, business register, or competent state authority of the corporate founder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization in accordance with the country of origin authentication regime

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter on the corporate founder and the ultimate beneficial owner, including account history verification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Regulated banking institution of the founder/UBO in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization in accordance with the country of origin authentication regime

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record certificate or equivalent police clearance certificate for each individual director and UBO where required by the Luxembourg notary or the AML/CFT risk assessment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National criminal records authority or competent law-enforcement authority of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization in accordance with the country of origin authentication regime

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified French translation of all non-French corporate, identity, address, and banking documents forming the incorporation bundle
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sworn/certified translator included on the official list of translators maintained by the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified translation accompanying the original apostilled or consular-legalized documents; no separate apostille is required on the translation itself

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all ultimate beneficial owners, directors, officers, and authorized signatories against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UN Security Council consolidated lists, and Luxembourg national administrative sanctions and AML/CFT notifications; mandatory heightened due diligence for domestic and foreign politically exposed persons (PEPs) in accordance with FATF Recommendation 12 and the Law of 12 November 2004, as amended; verification of the full ownership and control chain through the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners and foreign corporate registries; screening against the U.S. OFAC SDN List applied as a group policy and best-practice standard given the proposed USDC cryptocurrency payment rail and potential U.S. counterparties; ongoing transaction monitoring, source-of-funds verification, and a five-year statutory record-retention obligation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) at rcs.lu, governed by the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be written in Latin-script letters and Arabic numerals; French is the principal working language of the RCS and of notarial deeds, while Luxembourgish, French, and German are the official national languages. Non-French corporate names are admissible provided they are distinctive and not misleading, but a French rendering must be used in the notarial deed where the name is in a foreign language. Names originating in non-Latin scripts (e.g., Chinese characters) must be transliterated into Latin script and must use Arabic numerals for any numeric elements. The legal form indicator 'SARL' or 'Société à responsabilité limitée' must appear in the company name pursuant to Article 158-1 of the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / Banque / Crédit — requires prior license or authorization from the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
Assurance / Réassurance / Insurance — requires prior authorization from the Commissariat aux Assurances (CAA)
SICAV / SICAF / Fonds d'investissement / OPC / Véhicule d'investissement collectif — requires prior CSSF approval or supervised status
Société de Participations Financières (SPF) — reserved to entities incorporated under the specific supervised SPF regime
Bourse / Securities Exchange / Trading Platform — requires prior CSSF authorization
Audit / Réviseur d'Entreprises / Commissaire aux Comptes — reserved to firms approved by the CSSF and registered with the Institut des Réviseurs d'Entreprises
Avocat / Notaire / Huissier de Justice — reserved to members of the regulated legal professions
Grand-Duché / État / Gouvernement / Administration publique — words implying official connection with the State or a public authority are prohibited absent statutory authorization
Chambre de Commerce / Chamber of Skilled Trades — official body names protected by statute

Any name that is identical or confusingly similar to an existing RCS-registered name, a protected trademark, or an international organization, and any name contrary to public policy (ordre public) or good morals
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must first obtain the written reasons from the Luxembourg Business Registers; the notary may then promptly file a formal request for reconsideration with the RCS, which is adjudicated on administrative review. If the refusal is maintained, an action for annulment may be lodged with the Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) within three months of notification pursuant to the amended Law of 21 June 1999 on administrative procedure. Legal counsel may simultaneously file a fresh name-reservation request under a modified name to avoid delay; a name reservation is valid for 90 days and may not be extended as a matter of right, so a renewed reservation request must be refiled upon expiry after a fresh availability check.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not permissible as the statutory seat. The SARL must maintain a real, physical registered office at an actual street address in Luxembourg, which may correspond either to the central administration of the company or to the statutory seat. A post-office box alone is insufficient. External domiciliation through a commercial domiciliary agent licensed under the Law of 31 May 1999 on the domiciliation of companies is permitted, subject to a written domiciliation agreement and the filing of the domiciliary's written acceptance with the Luxembourg Business Registers. The domiciliation arrangement must be substantively genuine for corporate, VAT, and direct-tax purposes, particularly for a non-resident-owned virtual-event company, and cannot consist merely of a virtual mail-forwarding address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection is approximately 3-7% per fiscal year for a standard low-risk virtual-concert hosting entity with a resident director and adequate substance; the risk rises to 10-15% where the company relies exclusively on a licensed domiciliary address without resident management or local records; exposure is further elevated where USDC or other cryptocurrency payment rails are used, given heightened AML/CFT supervisory attention. Unannounced visits may be conducted by the Administration des Contributions Directes in tax-residency audits, by the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) for employer registration and payroll substance checks, and by the CSSF in AML/CFT inspections where the entity interacts with supervised financial intermediaries.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Paid-in minimum share capital of the SARL (EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and paid up before execution of the notarial deed; deposited into a blocked bank account or notarial escrow account)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg credit institution or the notary's escrow account; credited to the SARL's statutory share capital
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory minimum capital requirement under Article 158-1 et seq. of the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies; refundable equity, not a governmental fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial authentication of the articles of association (statuts) and execution of the incorporation deed for the SARL
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary (notaire) in the relevant judicial arrondissement
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory official notarial tariff (tarif officiel des notaires) plus notarial disbursements; prevailing market range EUR 500-1,200 for a standard SARL incorporation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the SARL in the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS) via the Luxembourg Business Registers electronic filing system
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory LBR filing fee schedule for registration of a commercial company

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official publication of the incorporation deed and registration particulars in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory publication tariff fixed by the Luxembourg Business Registers

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing of the beneficial ownership declaration in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) and issuance of the RBE registration receipt
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary filing the RBE return, and the Luxembourg Business Registers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Administrative charge covering notarial filing service and RBE statutory processing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille and/or consular legalization of founder identity, address, corporate good-standing, bank, and police-clearance documents originating outside Luxembourg
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority of each country of origin and/or the competent Luxembourg Embassy or Consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory or consular tariff approximating EUR 20-30 per apostille unit; consular fees vary by post

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation of the full incorporation bundle (identity documents, corporate extracts, address proofs, banking referrals, and contracts) by a sworn translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator authorized by the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate of EUR 50-90 per page for certified legal translation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and licensed commercial domiciliation services for the first fiscal year, including physical address, mail handling, registered-agent functions, and acceptance filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Luxembourg commercial domiciliary agent under the Law of 31 May 1999
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of EUR 1,200-2,500 per year for a standard domiciliation and substance package

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT pre-incorporation compliance file: UBO piercing, PEP determination, EU/UN/OFAC sanctions screening, source-of-wealth verification, and risk-assessment memorandum
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg AML compliance provider and designated AML counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a low-risk standard customer file; fixed fee quoted by the compliance provider

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), as amended — Title VII (SARL), Articles 710-1 to 710-8 (formation, minimum capital, RCS registration), Article 710-7 (notarial or private deed), Article 710-17 (publication in RESA); Law of 15 May 2024 on digitalisation and modernisation of company law, in force since 30 November 2024.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Legal Certainty Department (Département de la Sécurité juridique), Luxembourg City.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif (Deed of Incorporation) with annexed Statuts (Articles of Association), filed electronically with the RCS and published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum fully paid-up share capital of EUR 12,000, 100% subscribed and paid in cash at incorporation; each share must have a nominal value of EUR 1 or a multiple thereof. The funds must be blocked for the account of the SARL in a Luxembourg credit institution or deposited with the Caisse de Consignation, evidenced by a blocking certificate (attestation de blocage) which is released only upon RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The shareholders and directors, acting unanimously, RESOLVE: (1) that the Company's initial share capital of EUR 12,000 having been fully subscribed and paid up in cash, the shares are allotted to the subscribers as set out in the Articles of Association; (2) that the registered office is fixed at the Company's seat in the Commune of Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, and the Articles of Association are adopted; (3) that [Name] is appointed Manager (Gérant) with sole signature power for an indefinite term; and (4) that the Manager is authorised to complete RCS, RESA, tax, VAT, social security and banking registrations and to open merchant payment accounts required for the Company's virtual concert and metaverse ticketing business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Non-Confusion and Corporate Name Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — RCS online portal (lbregister.lu extranet)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search in the RCS index and file an application for a negative certificate (certificat de non-confusion) confirming that the proposed corporate name does not conflict with existing registered companies or protected trade names. Submit the planned Articles of Association for consistency review and pay the name-reservation fee.
required_dossiers: Proposed Articles of Association (draft)
Negative certificate application form
Identity documents of future shareholders and managers
Name reservation fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS objects on the ground of name conflict, the applicant selects an alternative name and re-files within 15 days; a third-party trademark holder may provide a notarised consent, or the applicant may appeal the refusal to the District Court (Tribunal de l'arrondissement) within two months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Statuts and Governance Instruments (Notarial Preparation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Notaire luxembourgeois) with corporate legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Luxembourg notary to draft the deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) and Statuts, including corporate governance provisions (management by one or more Gérants, general meeting rights, share transfer restrictions, fiscal year, profit distribution). Prepare the financial plan (plan financier) covering the first three years and the managers' eligibility declarations (déclaration de non-condamnation).
required_dossiers: Draft Statuts and deed of incorporation
Financial plan for the first three years
Statutory declaration of non-conviction for each proposed manager
Power of attorney if a signatory cannot appear in person
Passport copies and proof of residential address of shareholders and managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or the Luxembourg Bar flags a non-standard governance clause, the draft is revised and re-certified; if a manager has a foreign criminal record, a reasoned eligibility opinion is obtained or the manager is replaced before signature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Deposit and Blocking Certificate (Attestation de Blocage)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (e.g., BCEE, BIL) or Caisse de Consignation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked company account in the name of the future SARL and deposit the full minimum capital of EUR 12,000 as cash contributions from the subscribers. Obtain the banker's blocking certificate (attestation de blocage) confirming that the funds are irrevocably blocked in favour of the company and will be released exclusively upon production of the RCS registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Subscription statements executed by each shareholder
Draft Statuts showing the share capital and allotment
Identification of beneficial owners and authorised signatories
Anti-money laundering documentation and source-of-funds evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank defers the certificate due to outstanding KYC queries, the applicant provides a complete source-of-funds explanation; alternatively, the capital is deposited with the Caisse de Consignation (State depository) under Article 710-8 and the consignation receipt is submitted in lieu of the bank certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Deed of Incorporation before a Luxembourg Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before a Luxembourg notary to execute the acte constitutif and Statuts. The notary verifies the full subscription and payment of the capital, the legality of the clauses, and the capacity of the signatories. Shareholders acting remotely must grant a notarised power of attorney. The notary retains original signatures and authenticates the certified copies for subsequent filings.
required_dossiers: Finalised Statuts and deed of incorporation
Bank blocking certificate (original or certified copy)
Financial plan
Notarial fee receipt
Original powers of attorney for non-appearing shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a shareholder fails to appear, the deed is postponed and a fresh proxy is executed; if the notary detects a defect in the capital evidence or clauses, the parties sign an addendum (avenant) before the filing step.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration and RESA Statutory Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Legal Certainty Department; electronic filing performed by the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary electronically transmits the incorporation file to the RCS within 15 days of signature. The RCS registers the SARL, assigns the registration number (B-XXXXXX), issues the extract (extrait du RCS), and forwards the file for mandatory publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA). The company number automatically feeds the national tax databases.
required_dossiers: Incorporation deed (certified copy)
Full Statuts
Declaration of managers and registered office address
Bank blocking certificate (annex)
RCS e-filing authorisation and fee payment confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a deficiency notice (demande de complément), the notary files corrected documents within one month; if registration is refused, the company may appeal to the District Court within two months of the refusal notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, and Social Security Registration with State Authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD); Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AED); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the RCS data feed has automatically registered the SARL for corporate income tax (CIT) and municipal business tax (IBT). Submit the VAT registration form to the AED for the digital services activity, including the e-services and OSS regime where applicable, and register the platform's DAC7 reporting duty for virtual event sellers. Register as an employer with the CCSS and subscribe mandatory health and pension insurance before the first employee is hired.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Certified copy of the Articles of Association
Identities of officers and shareholders (natural persons)
Registered office lease agreement or proof of address
Bank account identification for tax refunds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax or VAT numbers are delayed, the appointed fiscal agent files provisional registrations and informs the AED; any late-filing penalty is cured by payment of the minimal default and submission of a justification letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Governance Directive, Licensing Due-Diligence, and Operational Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Managers / General Meeting; Ministry of the Economy (Direction générale des classes moyennes); Administration de l'Environnement; Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the First Board of Managers meeting adopting the pro-forma resolution (share subscription, registered office, officers). Approve the share register and open operational merchant accounts (Stripe, USDC/stablecoin settlement). Obtain written confirmation from the Ministry of the Economy that no establishment authorisation (autorisation d'établissement) applies to the virtual concert/metaverse ticketing activity. Secure occupational health and safety clearance from the ITM for the office premises and confirm the environmental exemption status with the Administration de l'Environnement.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma first board resolution (minutes)
Share register and shareholder ledger
Registered office lease agreement
Environmental exemption/EIA status notice from Administration de l'Environnement
Fire safety and occupational health clearance documents
AML/KYB file for payment service providers (Stripe / USDC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ITM or municipal fire safety inspection identifies deficiencies, corrective works are performed and a re-inspection is scheduled; if the Ministry of Economy questions the activity classification, a descriptive memorandum referencing ISIC 7110 and virtual event hosting is filed and a letter of exception is requested.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Determination authority: Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie), Direction générale des classes moyennes — 'Autorisation d'établissement' unit. Under the Law of 2 September 2011, no establishment permit is required because the ISIC 7110 virtual concert and metaverse ticketing activity constitutes a digital service outside the regulated artisan, commercial, and restaurateur professions.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required — no industrial operating licence (autorisation d'établissement) applies to this digital virtual-event hosting service; only standard commercial registration with the RCS and tax authorities is required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Environment Agency), Luxembourg — Direction du Droit Environnemental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no classified installation under the Law of 10 June 1999 on 'établissements classés'; an EIA report or registration is not applicable to purely virtual/metaverse service operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to operations; general compliance with municipal waste and water ordinances for office premises; if third-party data centres are leased, the EU Code of Conduct for Data Centre Energy Efficiency applies on a voluntary basis; no wastewater, VOC, or hazardous-waste discharge thresholds are triggered.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety conformity of the registered office under the Commune of Luxembourg fire prevention regulations (Service d'incendie et de secours), including smoke detectors, evacuation signage, and annual fire-safety audits; occupational health and safety clearance by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) before employees occupy the premises; mandatory employer registration with the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) for workplace accident coverage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct corporate taxes and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; unified electronic filing access through MyGuichet.lu (professional e-space) and the Luxembourg Business Registers portal (lbr.lu) for company registration and identification numbers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate the SARL before a Luxembourg notary and file the articles of association with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) to obtain the company's business identification number (matricule d'identification / numéro d'immatriculation). 2. Use the matricule as the statutory tax identification number (TIN) for direct tax purposes; no separate corporate TIN is issued. 3. Register for VAT by filing the VAT registration form (Formulaire 310) with the AEDT through the e-TVA/MyGuichet professional portal, annexing articles of association, proof of registered office in Luxembourg (or local VAT agent appointment for non-resident businesses), and RCS extract. 4. The AEDT allocates a Luxembourg VAT number with the prefix 'LU' followed by 8 digits; VAT registration confirmation is served electronically. 5. If the SARL is formed as a foreign entity acquiring local substance, simultaneous registration for employer formalities (Social Security Centre / CNPD) may be triggered, but these are administratively separate from the fiscal TIN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: a Luxembourg-resident SARL is a fully taxable corporate entity subject to unlimited tax liability on worldwide profits, comprising corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) and net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune), at a combined headline CIT rate of approximately 24.94% in Luxembourg City; no fiscal transparency/pass-through eligibility is available for an SARL under standard law, and non-resident shareholders are not regarded as taxable co-entrepreneurs.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not apply US-style check-the-box elections; entity classification follows commercial legal form. Available statutory elections include: (i) optional group taxation (fiscal unity / régime de groupe) for a resident parent and qualifying 95%-held resident subsidiaries; (ii) participation-exemption formalities (80% of dividends and capital gains exempt, subject to holding/recording conditions met at the time of disposal); (iii) IP box opt-in granting an 80% exemption on qualifying IP-derived income; (iv) VAT grouping election for closely linked Luxembourg entities; and (v) OSS registration elections (Union OSS for intra-EU B2C digital services and non-Union OSS for extra-EU services). ATAD hybrid mismatch provisions (Law of 23 December 2019) restrict deductible-payment and double-deduction outcomes, and Luxembourg has not implemented a separate hybrid-mismatch filing election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA – taxe sur la valeur ajoutée) implemented pursuant to the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979, as amended, and Council Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No registration threshold applies to non-established foreign businesses: any taxable supply or reverse-charge transaction in Luxembourg triggers mandatory VAT registration from the first euro. Resident small businesses may claim the Art. 57 exemption where annual turnover does not exceed EUR 35,000 (exclusive of VAT), with a right to opt for normal taxation. For intra-EU distance sales of goods and B2C supply of digital services, the Union-wide annual threshold is EUR 10,000 below which Luxembourg VAT at domestic rates applies; above the threshold, the destination-state VAT must be collected through the Union OSS scheme.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: B2G e-invoicing is mandatory in Luxembourg with invoices exchanged through the PEPPOL network. On 27 March 2025 the Council of Government approved a draft law introducing mandatory issuance of structured e-invoices for domestic B2B supplies from 1 January 2027 and for B2C transactions starting 1 January 2028; the system will operate on the national e-DELTA exchange platform with interoperability through PEPPOL. Luxembourg currently applies a post-audit control model rather than real-time fiscal clearance: no continuous transaction controls or tax-authority electronic stamping exist, but taxpayers must report SAF-T accounting files in XML upon request and file periodic VAT returns (Formulaire TVA) electronically on a monthly, quarterly or annual basis depending on turnover.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under Art. 42 of the Luxembourg VAT Law applies to: (i) direct supplies of goods dispatched or transported to a destination outside the EU; (ii) supplies of goods subsequently exported within 24 months in connection with contract work; and (iii) services directly linked to exported goods (transport, loading, storage, handling) and international transport services. For the virtual-concert business model: B2B digital-event services supplied to an EU customer fall outside Luxembourg VAT by virtue of the Art. 44 place-of-supply rule (taxed at customer establishment under reverse charge); B2C digital-event services to EU consumers are taxable at the destination-state rate and reportable through the OSS scheme; B2C services to non-EU consumers are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT (no Luxembourg VAT, no export zero-rating claim required). Zero-rating of physical goods requires commercial and documentary proof of export, must be evidenced before the AEDT on request, and the supplier must hold full records at the moment of invoicing.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration - Single Administrative Document (SAD) lodged in the Luxembourg/European AE Surface System (AES) showing the exporter as declarant and MRN reference
Entry in the exporter's records (EiR) or customs warehouse/authorised-economic-operator clearance evidence
Bill of Lading (ocean), CMR international consignment note (road), or Air Waybill (air) evidencing dispatch from the EU
Commercial invoice expressly referencing the Luxembourg VAT number and the Art. 42 zero-rate application
Proof of EU exit: customs barcode, exit summary declaration receipt, or transport-document destination stamp confirming arrival outside the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate or counterpart bank SWIFT/MT103 evidence showing export proceeds credited to the Luxembourg SARL account within the prescribed period
Export customer purchase order, contract and delivery confirmation identifying the non-EU customer as invoice recipient
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT conducts post-clearance audits with a standard five-year limitation period, extended to ten years for fraudulent conduct, during which export-supporting documentation must be produced; absence of documentary proof causes the 0% rate to be reversed and VAT at 17% becomes due. Administrative fines under Arts. 183-185 of the VAT Law range from EUR 250 to EUR 50,000 (up to EUR 250,000 for wilful violations), and late-payment interest accrues at the statutory legal rate applied to additional assessments. Deliberate fraudulent export zero-rating constitutes tax fraud (escroquerie fiscale) under the General Tax Law and VAT-specific provisions, punishable by criminal fines and imprisonment of up to five years, with possible publication of the conviction and disqualification of directors; clawback assessments may retroactively reach the entire ten-year period for fraud and are secured by a legal lien on the taxpayer's movable assets.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) acting within the Eurosystem; banking supervision is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). Luxembourg maintains no independent exchange-control institution; capital movements are governed by Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and Directive 88/361/EEC, and no foreign-exchange approval or licensing authority exists for ordinary current or capital transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro (EUR) is fully convertible on both current account and capital account for a Luxembourg SARL. Profit remittance and dividend distribution are legally unrestricted; the only outbound frictions are the standard Luxembourg dividend withholding tax (15% domestic, reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for a qualifying parent company, or to reduced treaty rates) and normal tax-residence documentation. No import/export licences, no repatriation authorisations, and no limitations on holding foreign-currency accounts apply to an ISIC 7110 virtual-performance entity. Non-resident ownership is permitted and does not affect convertibility. All cross-border payments above the EUR 12,500 statistical threshold must be reported by the resident bank to the BCL for balance-of-payments purposes, but this is a statistical filing, not a control measure.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender timeline, no minimum conversion ratio, and no repatriation quota for export receipts or service revenues. The SARL may freely retain USD, USDC-proceeds converted to fiat, or any other permitted currency in a bank or regulated VASP account. The only obligation is bookkeeping and prudential valuation: cash balances in foreign currency must be revalued at each closing date under Luxembourg GAAP (Lux GAAP), and any crypto-asset holdings in USDC that remain unconverted for more than one day must be recognised at fair value with an impairment test, triggering no regulatory capital charge but creating balance-sheet volatility.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué) plus Operational EUR Current Account
Capital Escrow Account plus Operational EUR Current Account with Multi-Currency
Operational EUR Current Account plus Capital Escrow Account
Operational EUR Current Account plus Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility under strict constraints. An EU/EEA-authorised electronic money institution or payment institution may passport into Luxembourg under PSD2 (Directive (EU) 2015/2366) and provide SEPA, card acquiring and payment-initiation services to the SARL; Stripe, acting through its Irish-authorised payment institution, is fully viable for card and SEPA collection into an IBAN. However, the target rail 'Cryptocurrency_USDC' is outside the scope of an EMI licence: an EMI cannot accept, custody or convert USDC without itself holding a Luxembourg VASP registration (Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering, as amended, and CSSF guidance on virtual assets) or without using a separate regulated crypto-custodian. Offshore non-EEA EMIs (UK, Singapore, UAE) have no EU passport and would require either a Luxembourg branch authorisation or an EU partner-EMI arrangement; practical onboarding of such an entity as the sole bank is Low. The recommended structure is: (i) Stripe Ireland for fiat card/SEPA rails; (ii) a German or Luxembourg-licensed crypto-custodian (e.g., a Bafin-authorised crypto bank or a CSSF-registered VASP) for USDC receipt and immediate EUR conversion; and (iii) a tier-1 Luxembourg bank as the master settlement account, receiving only EUR.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical meeting with the authorised signatory (gérant) is standard at BCEE and BIL for the initial account opening, and the non-resident beneficial owner must undergo identification regardless of the manager's presence. Remote onboarding via video-verified KYC is legally permissible under the CSSF AML/CFT framework (regulation 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended, and CSSF guidance on non-face-to-face identification), subject to each bank's risk appetite; in practice, BIL and BCEE permit a hybrid path where the manager completes a video interview and the notarised corporate documents are delivered via apostille and by the Luxembourg registered agent. A newly incorporated SARL with metaverse tokenization exposure will very likely be required to schedule one in-person visit in Luxembourg or to appoint a Luxembourg-resident authorised signatory or a CSSF-licensed fiduciary to co-sign, but full remote-only opening is possible at BNP Paribas Luxembourg for low-risk clients if the UBO has a verifiable banking lineage.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO with no Luxembourg nexus, combined with a crypto-adjacent virtual-concert revenue model (USDC ticketing tokenization)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) extract; LEI certificate; notarised articles of association with the capital-payment certificate; shareholder register and ultimate-ownership chain; source-of-funds documentation for the entire share capital (six months of bank statements, wealth-formation explanation, prior tax returns of the UBO); a three-year business plan with unit economics and a named merchant-of-record; platform proof (signed artist/venue contracts, domain registration, ticketing engine screenshots); bank reference from a major bank in the UBO's residence jurisdiction; professional CVs of directors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Characterisation of virtual-event ticket sales as unlicensed e-money issuance, payment service operation, or secondary-market trading / scalping
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion from a Luxembourg avocat confirming the activity constitutes a general professional service (ISIC 7110) outside the scope of the Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services and electronic money, and outside the gambling licensing regime; the end-user terms with a refund and cancellation policy; representation that the SARL does not issue redeemable stored-value instruments; a clear statement that all fan payments are collected as fiat via an authorised PSP, or as USDC only when instant-converted by a licensed VASP acting as principal.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: USDC inflows received without the SARL holding a Luxembourg VASP registration
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A structured service agreement with an EU-licensed VASP or crypto-bank (Bafin or CSSF supervised) under which the SARL never holds private keys and the USDC is automatically swept and converted to EUR at the VASP within the same settlement day; a sanctions-screening output from a recognised screening tool covering the fan-base IP geography; confirmation that the SARL itself engages in no exchange, custody, or conversion own-book activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and payments-traffic exposure from a worldwide metaverse audience (potential OFAC/EU sanctions breaches through ticket purchases)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Compliance manual including an IP-based geoblocking policy excluding EU/OFAC-sanctioned territories; daily sanctions-screening logs from World-Check or Dow Jones; contractual warranties from the payment processor requiring the processor to enforce its own restricted-party list; optional IP-geoblocking of United States ticket purchases pending a state-by-state securities-law review of tokenized access rights; CRM records evidencing customer due diligence for premium package buyers above EUR 10,000.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The SARL minimum capital (EUR 12,000; practical working capital EUR 50,000–150,000) must be transferred from the shareholder's own bank account as a SWIFT MT103 or SEPA Credit Transfer to the Luxembourg notary's escrow account with remittance field 70 stating 'Capital subscription — Cash contribution for subscription of shares of LU_SARL pursuant to notarised deed dated [date]'. The receiving bank will classify the payment as 'Direct Investment — Equity Capital' for BCL balance-of-payments statistics; aggregate inflows above EUR 12,500 are automatically reported, with no prior exchange-control approval. The structure must be share capital, not shareholder loan, to avoid the notary certification of contribution difficulties; if a shareholder loan is used, a signed written loan agreement is mandatory for amounts above EUR 350,000 to prevent thin-capitalisation recharacterisation, and the interest rate must be at arm's length and subject to Lux GAAP accrual. USDC proceeds are not acceptable as a capital contribution: a Luxembourg notary requires actual book-money credit in a bank account or a certified bank transfer; therefore, the UBO must convert any crypto to EUR through a regulated exchange and execute the bank transfer from the same beneficial-owner account to preserve a clean audit trail.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Recommended clearing rails in order of hierarchy: (1) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) for all EU/EEA artist, licensor and infrastructure payments — next-day settlement with zero marginal cost and a full audit trail in the bank statement; (2) SEPA Instant (SCT Inst) for sub-EUR 100,000 royalty splits requiring same-second value; (3) SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA outbound royalties (e.g., US/UK artists), with field 70 containing the invoice reference and field 72 stating 'BEN ONLY' to push all charges to the beneficiary; no Luxembourg currency-approval requirement attaches to any outbound payment; (4) Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP600) are legally permissible but economically sub-optimal for service-based virtual-concert royalties and should be reserved for platform-technology co-production contracts exceeding EUR 500,000 where a performance guarantee is required; (5) USDC outbound payments are not a recognised settlement rail under Luxembourg law: if a contract obligates a crypto-denominated payout, the obligation should be net-settled by the EU-licensed VASP converting EUR to USDC at the beneficiary's request, with the SARL's own bank account remaining EUR-only; (6) all outbound disbursements must be supported by an underlying invoice, signed contract, and beneficial-owner attestations retained for at least five years under CSSF record-keeping obligations; a standing payment-authorisation matrix with dual control above EUR 10,000 is expected by the onboarding bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla EUR/USD FX forward with a Luxembourg credit institution, maximum tenor 12 months, executed only against a contracted pipeline of US-stadium or USD-denominated ticketing settlements, documented in the SARL treasury policy and subject to a bank ISDA/CSA or master FX agreement
FX swap (FXS) for temporary EUR/USD bridging of settlement timing gaps between Stripe payout dates, artist disbursement dates, and USDC conversion dates
European-style foreign-exchange option (EUR call / USD put) to hedge a committed multi-month global artist tour schedule without locking in an unfavourable forward rate

Cross-currency interest-rate swap (CCIRS) only where the share-capital injection is ultimately financed by a USD-denominated parent loan converted to EUR; the swap must be plain-vanilla, non-leveraged, and aligned with the EU Benchmark Regulation and EMIR clearing thresholds

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are technically permissible under Luxembourg law but are not a prudential instrument for EUR/USD because the euro is fully deliverable under the single-currency regime; if an NDF is proposed for an inconvertible market currency arising from ticket reseller receipts, the bank will require a written commercial-risk dossier proving genuine exposure, otherwise it will be treated as speculative and declined under the SARL's treasury mandate

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Filing (Dépôt des Comptes Annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the financial year end; for a calendar-year SARL, by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered daily penalty (astreinte) up to €250 per day after formal notice; administrative fines up to €5,000; continued failure after approximately 6 months may lead to RCS criminal referral and strike-off (radiation).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Declaration Confirmation (Confirmation Annuelle des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) – Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between 1 October and 31 December of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties of €1,250–€5,000; criminal fines for deliberate false declaration or omission up to €250,000; registration suspension or RCS strike-off in recurrent default cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) and Adoption of Accounts (Approbation des Comptes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate record – minutes kept at registered office; not filed with RCS unless specifics required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be held within 6 months after the financial year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil liability of directors and potential nullity of resolutions if accounts are adopted late; does not directly trigger RCS strike-off but may expose the SARL to court-ordered liquidation in extreme non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for a Luxembourg SARL when it exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds at two consecutive balance sheet dates: balance sheet total €4,400,000; net turnover €8,800,000; average number of full-time employees over the financial year = 50.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Plan Comptable Normalisé) as set out in the Luxembourg law of 19 December 2002; IFRS is mandatory for consolidated accounts of publicly traded entities and may be voluntarily applied by certain consolidated groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A Luxembourg SARL must annually confirm the accuracy of its beneficial owner information with the RCS using the official electronic UBO filing platform between 1 October and 31 December, regardless of whether a shareholding transfer occurred. Any share transfer or other event modifying beneficial ownership must additionally be reported to the RCS within one month of the company becoming aware of the change; the updated UBO declaration must reflect the new ownership structure and the share register must be amended accordingly.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Managers (Registre des Gérants et Administrateurs)
Register of Share Transfers and Acquisitions (Registre des Cessions)
Register of Charges and Collateral (Registre des Nantissements)
Minute Book of Shareholders and Board Meetings (Procès-Verbaux)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate for Luxembourg City (17% corporate income tax, 7% solidarity surcharge, 6.75% municipal business tax); reduced 15% CIT applies to first EUR 175,000 of taxable income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 80% exemption on qualifying net intellectual property income (resulting effective rate approx. 4.99%); notional interest deduction on qualifying new equity; participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains; small business exemptions are not relevant for a SARL.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 500 (Déclaration d'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) filed jointly with municipal business tax return and net wealth tax return, via the eCDF module on MyGuichet.lu (LuxTrust authentication).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (financial year; no quarterly instalments for CIT; advance VAT and payroll obligations remain separate).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is 30 June following the tax year; filed electronically under the ACD portal with possible extension to 31 December where the taxpayer is represented by a registered tax adviser.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal form SARL, registered office, RCS Luxembourg number, corporate taxpayer number (matricule), fiscal period, business activity code (NAICS 711310).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the Luxembourg VAT and income tax numbers; foreign beneficial owners need not be disclosed unless they are directors or controlling shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Insert profit or loss per statutory accounts, adjust for non-deductible expenses, exempt IP income, tax credits, notional interest deduction, and loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach separate schedules for transactions with non-resident affiliates and substantiate arm's length treatment of virtual concert licensing, token fees and platform commissions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 – Tax credits and withholding tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate foreign-source income, gross foreign tax withheld, and DTA credits claimed against Luxembourg CIT for virtual concert rights and ticket processing income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Tax Residence Certificate and completed Form 190 to substantiate each foreign withholding tax credit; no credit is allowed for income sheltered by the IP box regime.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an automatic late filing penalty of up to EUR 250 and a 10% ex officio assessment surcharge; late payment bears monthly interest of 0.6% (7.2% p.a.); wilful false declarations are criminal under Art. 426 LIR and may result in fines and imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% domestic rate on dividend distributions; 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying shareholders holding at least 10% for 12 continuous months; DTA rates generally 5% to 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Beneficial owner must submit an advance withholding tax relief request to the ACD (via MyGuichet/eCDF) before distribution, supported by a valid Tax Residence Certificate, confirmation of beneficial ownership, and, where applicable, EU Directive compliance; exchange-of-information approval required for non-EU treaty residents.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: No Luxembourg domestic WHT on outbound royalties or arm's-length interest to non-residents; under DTAs rates are commonly 0% for royalties and 0%-10% for interest, subject to beneficial ownership and substance conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50,000,000 consolidated group revenue triggers mandatory Master File and Local File; Country-by-Country Report is applicable when the consolidated group exceeds EUR 750,000,000; no specific transaction threshold for non-arm's-length adjustments.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No stand-alone ESR statute; substance analysis is applied through Luxembourg GAAR and the OECD Multilateral Convention. The SARL must demonstrate real decision-making, adequate employees, office, bank account, and risk-taking in metaverse event operations; failing this, income may be recharacterised, treaty relief denied, and the SARL treated as a conduit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-reporting or concealing gross receipts from virtual concert ticketing, including cryptocurrency (USDC) token sales from metaverse events.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalty under Art. 426 of the Luxembourg General Tax Law: fine of up to EUR 25,000 or imprisonment up to 5 years (or both); civil tax assessment up to 100% of evaded tax and monthly default interest of 0.6%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for evaded tax where they knew or should have known; convictions trigger travel bans, asset freezes, publication of judgement and civil restitution to the tax administration.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Luxembourg SARL with no retained management, no staff, and no substantive activity as a mere conduit for IP royalties and ticket income sourced from virtual performances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative recharacterisation of the SARL as a documentary shell; denial of DTA benefits, loss of Luxembourg treaty protection, retroactive assessment and 10% to 100% penalties plus reclassification of amounts as constructively distributed dividends.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors appointed to enable the shell arrangement face civil liability for unwound distributions and potential criminal liability for false declarations; Luxembourg courts may issue travel bans and prohibit holding corporate offices for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare Master File or Local File for cross-border intercompany transactions (licensing of virtual concert technology, token processing, marketing fees) when the group exceeds the 50 million limit, or charging pricing that does not satisfy the arm's length standard.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment with consequential tax and net wealth tax; 7.2% p.a. late-payment interest; a penalty up to 10% of adjusted tax; non-production of documents after demand may be treated as tax obstruction with a further fine.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign transfer pricing documentation or knowingly approve non-arm's length arrangements become personally exposed to the administrative penalty and to damages; in egregious cases, indictment for tax fraud and travel restrictions are possible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / KYC Failure and Virtual Asset Facilitation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting Stripe or USDC payments for metaverse concert tickets without customer due diligence, suspicious-transaction reporting to the CRF (FIU), or maintenance of internal AML controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Breach of Luxembourg AML Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF regulations: fines against the SARL up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover for legal persons; suspension or revocation of licences; monitoring and compliance orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, as reporting officers, are personally liable for AML violations; sanctions include imprisonment up to 5 years, confiscation of proceeds, travel bans and bans from management, plus joint civil liability to the Supervisory Commission.
